collection: TBF1 Navy Letters - WWII letters of Ens. Thomas Frazier Beck, USNR
conventions: Original spelling and grammar kept. [?] = uncertain reading; [crossed out] = struck-through text; [bracketed letters] = text lost at scan edge. Dates in YYYY-MM-DD; a date marked '(probable)' was inferred from content. File paths are relative to the 'Family' folder. Where the same page was scanned more than once, the clearest scan was used and the others are listed in 'duplicate_and_misfiled_scans'.
content_warning: Several letters contain period racist, antisemitic and anti-Japanese language. It is transcribed verbatim as part of the historical record, and each affected letter carries a NOTE in its header.

people.Tom: Thomas Frazier Beck (b. Feb. 27, 1919, per letters). Karns City, PA. Penn State (commerce & finance); also studied at Pitt. V-7 midshipman at Columbia (John Jay Hall) July-Oct 1942; commissioned Ensign, USNR, Oct. 21, 1942. Amphibious Force: Solomons MD and Norfolk VA; LCI(L) 218 (Dec 1942 training); LCI(L) 345 (commissioned Jan 22, 1943, Houston); executive officer of USS LCI(L) 62 from Feb 3, 1943, in the South Pacific for about 13 months; back in the U.S. about Mar-Apr 1944; U.S. Naval Station, Grand Trunk Pier, Portland ME (1944-45); hospitalized for malaria about Apr-May 1945 (probably Portsmouth Naval Hospital).
people.Mother: Elva Beck (Mrs. John A. Beck), Karns City, PA. Served on the rationing board; later a company director ('Pres. of Beck, Inc.').
people.Dad: John A. Beck, Karns City, PA; apparently in the oil business. Seriously ill in Nov 1942; the letters strongly suggest he died around Dec 1942 or Jan 1943 (letters after that go to Mother only; a school memorial picture of Dad, 1943-05-11; 'When Dad's picture arrived...', 1943-12-17). Not stated outright, so worth verifying.
people.John: Tom's brother, and his 'financial adviser'. Married Fran in August 1943.
people.George: Tom's younger brother. At Allegheny College, then the Navy V-12 program (Lewisburg/Bucknell) from mid-1943.
people.Isabel (Izzy): Probably Tom's sister; considered teaching and the WAVES.
people.Janny: Tom's sister; attended PCW (Pennsylvania College for Women). Paired with Bill (Jameson).
people.Betty: Probably Tom's sister (her birthday is Jan. 5, 'a big day for the Becks'); visited Tom at Solomons Nov 1942. Married to or connected with John/Dick; relationships are not fully clear.
people.Marge / Margorie / Marjorie: Probably Tom's younger sister; a basketball player, birthday about May 27.
people.Jackie: A young child in the family.
people.Others: Uncle Paul, Uncle Frank, Uncle Chauncey, Uncle John & Libby, Aunts Helen, Hazel, Harriet, Lyle/Lyde, Bess; Luke & Lena; Adam (Moser); Bill Jameson; Geo. Wagenhorst; Chet Beard; Glenn Scott (Oil City); the McClungs; the Pelkeys (Olive & Bob); Lane (a friend in Portland, 1945).

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, New York, N.Y. (at Columbia University), room 1317 John Jay Hall
letters.notes: Tom's first letter from midshipman school, written on the day he arrived. The back gives his full name and mailing address: 'Thomas F. Beck AS-V7, USNR Midshipmens School, New York, New York, 1317 John Jay'. AS-V7 means Apprentice Seaman in the V-7 naval reserve officer program. He asks his family not to mention Columbia University on the envelope or he will get demerits. His roommate is O'Bryan (reading uncertain), an Irishman from Syracuse. A later note in blue ink in a different hand reads 'I wanted to see too [?] - John', perhaps from a family member who read the letter. The original-folder scan of pg1 also exists and is identical in resolution.

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York (bounds 110th-122nd St., Riverside Dr. to Morningside Dr.)
letters.notes: 4204XX.jpg in the parent folder is a second scan of page 4 of this letter; its filename date 'April 1942' is wrong. Written in pencil because the canteen ran out of ink. Tom describes the Pullman train ride, meeting a fellow from Indiana, Pa. (probably the 'boy from Indiana' with appendicitis in the 1942-07-27 letter), uniform sizes, drill, climbing 13 floors, Navy terms (deck, ladder, hold, mess, head), and a first course of about 3 weeks. He advises Mother to wait before visiting. Mentions Aunt Helen. The last line of pg1 and of pg3 are cut off in the scans.

other_dates_mentioned: 'My 4th' - July 4, 1942 (drill, a parade, and a USO show)
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom enclosed photos (not in this collection) of the men who roomed near him: Spooner (Toledo), McGuire (Conn.), Cramer (Indiana), and his roommate O'Brien. The photos were taken by a schoolteacher from Providence. Courses: math (review for Tom), ship types, and Naval Organization. Mother made two mistakes on the envelope: she mentioned Columbia and forgot his room number. 50 demerits gets a man 'bounced'. He gives mess-hour times for calling the pay phones and visiting hours. People named: Glenn Scott (Officer of the Deck), Geo. Wagemhorst (reading uncertain), Isabel (probably a family member).

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom passed his physical. There was a dance at the 'Prairie State' (USS Prairie State, the Midshipmen's School training ship moored on the Hudson), sponsored by the Navy League and the USO, with about 3 men per girl. He was stuck for two hours talking with a girl who couldn't dance. The indoctrination period was rumored to last 2-3 weeks before the men became midshipmen. He met Geo. Wagenhorst, who offered to help him. The postscript says he 'just left John', so John (probably a family member) was visiting New York; see the 1942-07-14 letter.

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: The laundry came back late and mixed up because the Navy-issued marking ink washed out. Tom asks Mother to send his plain white T-shirts. The indoctrination period ends this week with finals: high grades mean becoming a midshipman, average grades mean being checked for officer qualities, and low grades mean being 'bilged' (dismissed). Also mentions rowing, flag signaling, and a cold. He had a visit from John (probably a family member, and likely the 'John' who wrote the note on the back of the 1942-07-02 letter).

other_dates_mentioned: finals at the end of this week (about July 17-18, 1942)
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom answers letters from Adam and from 'Sis' together, which suggests Adam may be Sis's husband (a brother-in-law), though this is not stated. Tom compares the small bounds with 'being up in the mountains at State College', which suggests he had attended Penn State. The course was cut in half and finals are at the end of the week. Most of the men seem to be from the South. After a USO dance, he says he'll 'stick to the corn-fed' girls.

other_dates_mentioned: Monday (July 20, 1942) - starts school as a Midshipman
July 18, 1942 - Dick & Betty's wedding (Tom sent a telegram and couldn't attend)
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom finished his indoctrination exams and expects a 75-80 average. Irving Berlin and Sigmund Romberg were to entertain at that night's dance. Dick & Betty got married on or about this date; Tom sent a telegram. Betty appears to be his sister, and Dick her new husband, who was apparently also a V-7 candidate. He hints for cake, cookies, and pie from home, and asks Mother not to talk much about the school and courses.

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: The main course started today, and Tom expects to be sworn in as a midshipman within a day or two. His grades were 3.2 and 2.9 out of 4. About 900 men are in the class, with a percentage dismissed every 3 weeks (4 times in all). Liberty rules: Saturday night to Sunday evening within 50 miles; men 'on the tree' (below 2.5 in any course) get only Saturday night; demerits are marched off at 2 per hour. This explains the 'tree' reference in the 1942-07-27 letter.

other_dates_mentioned: To-morrow (July 23, 1942) - to be sworn in as midshipmen
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: First 'bilge': about 90 men dismissed that day, with 100 more expected before graduation. Tom's deck (13) lost 13 men, but both men in room 1313 stayed; the 1942-07-02 letter gives his room as 1317 John Jay, so he may have moved or misremembered. Communications is his toughest course: he knows the flags but not Morse code.

other_dates_mentioned: Yesterday (July 22, 1942) - shots and swearing-in as midshipmen
Saturday/Sunday (July 25-26, 1942) - planned trip downtown and possibly a ballgame
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom was sworn in as a midshipman along with 800 men at once, and received typhoid shots and vaccinations (several men passed out). He was issued his blue uniform, with white cap covers and stiff collars. Mother sent a newspaper article about the wedding (Dick & Betty's; see 1942-07-18). He describes watching Army transports, pursuit planes, and Flying Fortresses overhead.

other_dates_mentioned: Saturday/Sunday (July 25-26, 1942) - first leave: a radio broadcast and Radio City
August 1 (1942) - Bob Hines expected to be stationed there
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Page 1 (from the Adobe folder) completes the letter that was only partial in TBF0defective; the bottom line of pg1 is cut off in the scan. Tom started the letter in pencil 'on the sly' while standing watch in charge of the 7th deck, then switched to ink back in his room. On his first leave, people mistook the midshipmen for merchant marines. Mother and Dad planned a visit. Tom says he is from 'about 50 miles north' of Pittsburgh, near Butler and Karns City, PA; Armagost is from Rimersburg, PA. 'On the tree' means below 2.5 in a course (see 1942-07-20). 'The Eagle' is probably the Butler Eagle newspaper. People named: Armagost, 'the boy from Indiana' (appendicitis), Bob Hines.

other_dates_mentioned: Next Wednesday (Aug. 5, 1942) - graduation of midshipmen on the 'other ships'
August 11 (1942) - replacements arrive and another hall opens
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Second typhoid shot. Tom expects to be 'on the tree' in communications (blinker too slow). Mother had visited family in Wheeling (WV); Tom jokes that the Army has a larger grasp on the family than the Navy. He describes the USS Prairie State (the former battleship USS Illinois, a stationary training ship) and says he will decline a transfer to it.

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Isabel visited Tom; Janny had mentioned she was coming. Isabel and Janny are probably sisters or relatives (a later file is titled 'Z Janny PCW', possibly Pennsylvania College for Women). Mother sent a camera. Sunday watch runs 1700 Saturday to 1700 Sunday. Graduation is rumored for October 2. His first pay was $4.70 after deductions.

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom stayed off the tree and passed Captain's Inspection. The previous week he saw the Giants play the Cardinals, and he has a ticket to Yankee Stadium. About 1000 new men arrive next week. A water stain obscures a word or two on pg2.

other_dates_mentioned: Thursday-Sunday (Aug. 13-16, 1942) - Mother's planned visit and Tom's liberty times
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Arrangements for Mother's visit to New York. Tom lists the school's pay phone numbers (UNiversity 4-9273, 4-9539, 4-9635). John had a list of the numbers, and Isabel can explain the visiting rules (both had visited earlier).

other_dates_mentioned: October 13 (1942) - graduation date overheard from the commander
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Written just after Mother's weekend visit to New York. A rumored 'second front' turned out to be 'just a commando raid', almost certainly the Dieppe Raid of Aug. 19, 1942 (so the letter may be dated a day early or written late on the 19th). 16 men left, and 50-60 more are expected after first-term exams. Tom overheard that graduation would be October 13.

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, New York (inferred)
letters.notes: A short pencil note, probably the back of a postcard (part of a postmark shows at top right). Tom is having photo proofs sent home, probably the portraits he mentioned in the 1942-08-10 letter. Faint pencil, but readable.

other_dates_mentioned: next Saturday (Aug. 29, 1942) - Green Bay Packers vs. Brooklyn Dodgers football game
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: First-term exam schedule. Tom spent Saturday at Coney Island with O'Brien (his roommate, named in the 1942-07-08 letter). He plans to see the Green Bay Packers play the (Brooklyn) Dodgers football team.

other_dates_mentioned: September 1942 - planned visit from Betty and John
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Written in pencil during the seamanship & communications final; the instructor suggested writing letters home. Tom also took the navigation final that morning. Betty and John plan to visit in September. Here 'Betty and John' are a couple, while the 1942-07-18 letter mentions a wedding of 'Dick & Betty', so the relationships are unclear. He met men he knew from 'State' (Penn State) at Furnald Hall; 'One is a Beta' means a Beta Theta Pi fraternity member, suggesting Tom belonged to a rival fraternity. Midshipmen indoctrinated at Notre Dame moved into Johnson Hall.

other_dates_mentioned: Mother's birthday (shortly before Sept. 1; Tom forgot it)
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom apologizes for forgetting Mother's birthday, which was in late August. He is frustrated with poorly qualified instructors: 'If it wasn't for a few of the officers I would think I was at Polk', probably Polk State School, a Pennsylvania institution for the mentally disabled, used as a joke. The Adobe-folder file 420901pg2.jpg is mislabeled (it duplicates page 1); the real page 2 is 420901pg2.jpg in the parent folder.

letters.date_source: written on letter as '9 August 1942', but it refers to Labor Day (Sept. 7, 1942) as already past, so the month is probably a slip. The filename '420809' follows the written date. Confirmed by the 1942-09-13 postcard, which says 'the game yesterday [Sat. Sept. 12] was wonderful', matching this letter's 'next Saturday ... All-Star game'.
other_dates_mentioned: finals on the 15th & 16th, graduation on the 21st (September 1942)
next Saturday - review held at the All-Star game
Dec 31 & Jan 1 - finals for the next class at John Jay
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: The date is probably wrong on the letter itself (see date_source). The family spent the holiday 'at the Lake'. Tom's roommate was dismissed in the last bilge. An officer recruited for bomb disposal school, and Tom declined. The letter records antisemitic sentiment among the midshipmen after an announcement that Jewish midshipmen could go home for their holidays; it is transcribed as written for historical accuracy. Water stains on pg2 obscure a few letters.

letters.written_to: Mother (addressed to Mrs. John A. Beck, Karns City, Pa.)
letters.date_source: postmark (New York, N.Y., Sep 13 1942, 2:30 PM, Grand Central Annex)
other_dates_mentioned: yesterday (Sept. 12, 1942) - 'the game' (the All-Star game mentioned in the 1942-09-09 letter)
letters.location: New York City (mailed from Grand Central Annex); Tom was heading to Hackensack, NJ
letters.notes: KEY IDENTIFYING DOCUMENT: addressed to 'Mrs. John A. Beck, Karns City, Pa.', which confirms that Tom's mother was Mrs. John A. Beck (so his father was John A. Beck) and that the family home was Karns City, Pennsylvania. Servicemen's mail was sent postage-free ('Free' written in the stamp box). This is a Biltmore Hotel picture postcard. Pat Hill invited Tom to dinner in Hackensack (see 1942-09-17).

other_dates_mentioned: Sunday (Sept. 13, 1942) - dinner in Hackensack with Pat Hill and her aunt
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Graduation is rumored to be postponed to Oct. 28. Midshipmen must buy their officer uniforms, and the government gives $250 toward them. Mother ordered some of the portrait photos. Grandma McClung (reading uncertain) is ill, which is hard on 'Mr. McClung'. 'Speaking of McClung's I am getting anxious to see one of them. I hope he will remember me' may refer to a new baby in that family; this is unclear.

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: A parish priest arranged a weekend date with Powers models (the John Robert Powers modeling agency). 'Hickory' is a baby in the family who isn't walking yet; he is probably the McClung baby hinted at in the 1942-09-17 letter, perhaps a nephew. Isabel had written. Graduation has been extended to the 21st.

letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom has been advised to buy only the minimum uniforms, since some assignments wear overalls instead of khaki. Graduation may be held at Riverside Church. He was put 'on the tree' for the first time (2.4, where 2.5 is passing) by an instructor he dislikes. Navigation class is doing a theoretical 6-day Atlantic crossing, and ordnance training covers machine guns and 3-inch guns.

other_dates_mentioned: last night (Sept. 28, 1942) - phone call with Mother and Dad
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: KEY MILESTONE: Tom has been assigned to Amphibian (amphibious) school, where officers will be 'in charge of landing barges'. Most classmates are going to Norfolk; others to the West Coast, Florida, or Diesel school. None were assigned to big ships or even destroyers. He expects the 2nd front to come the next spring and hopes to command 'my own ship even tho it is a mud scow'. He asks Mother not to repeat this.

other_dates_mentioned: Oct. 3 (1942) - Saturday Evening Post issue with an article about the Navy
Saturday the 23rd (actually Oct. 24, 1942 was a Saturday) - a classmate's wedding to a girl from Warren, Ohio
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Tom recommends a Saturday Evening Post article (Oct. 3, 1942) about the Navy and amphibious tactics. About 400 men have their assignments, and Tom was among the first. Many dislike Amphibian school, but he thinks it's a good thing. He doesn't expect to need whites.

other_dates_mentioned: Wednesday morning the 21st (Oct. 21, 1942) - graduation at Riverside Church
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Graduation is confirmed for Wednesday morning, Oct. 21, 1942, at Riverside Church, with two invitations per man. Tom bought his uniforms through a Baltimore wholesaler, saving $50. Mother sent cookies, popcorn, and candy; Dad sent a letter and bank statements. A church program listed Paul M. Doty, Jr., possibly 'Doty from Chicora' (Chicora, PA, near Karns City). Paul M. Doty Jr. of Chicora later became a noted Harvard biochemist; he was at Columbia in 1942, which makes the identification plausible, though the letter does not confirm it.

other_dates_mentioned: Tomorrow (Oct. 10, 1942) - battalion review before an Admiral
letters.location: U.S. Naval Reserve Midshipmen's School, Columbia University, New York
letters.notes: Travel plans for graduation, by train to Pittsburgh or by car. Extra guest tickets are hard to get, but one pass admits a guest to a room where the ceremony is broadcast. A paragraph for Dad mentions Mr. Wasson (reading uncertain) and forms Tom signed. About 400 men will march as a battalion for an Admiral's review, and Tom made the front rank. Reveille is now 5:30 with a run before breakfast.

letters.date_source: inferred: 'commissioned today' at Riverside Church, and graduation was set for Wednesday, Oct. 21, 1942 (1942-10-05 letter)
letters.location: Riverside Church, New York City
letters.notes: KEY IDENTIFYING DOCUMENT: TOM'S FULL NAME IS THOMAS FRAZIER BECK, 'son of Mr. and Mrs. John A. Beck of Karns City' ('Frazier' matches the 'Frazier-McCafferty' package, 1943-12-06, perhaps a family connection). He was one of 753 ensigns commissioned as deck officers in the Naval Reserve after the 3-month V-7 course, in the Eighth Class, the largest V-7 class to date. Ceremony conducted by Capt. John K. Richards, USN; speaker Rear Adm. John Henry Newton. Includes his portrait in uniform.

letters.location: Bachelor Officers' Quarters, Naval Operating Base, Norfolk, Virginia
letters.notes: This is Tom's first letter after graduating and being commissioned (written on leftover Midshipmen's School stationery). He traveled with Chet by night boat to Norfolk. Chet knew someone in the OPA (Office of Price Administration) and a Lieutenant on the base. Of the new amphibious officers, the first 80 went to Little Creek, the next group to Solomons, and the rest (including Tom) stayed at Norfolk. Mailing address: Amphibious Force, Post Office, Hampton Roads Branch, Naval Operating Base, Norfolk, Virginia. The bottom of pg1 appears cut off in the scan, so a line may be missing between pages. There is no letter from the Oct. 21 graduation itself; Tom presumably went home on leave afterward.

letters.date_source: the letter says 'Wednesday 1943', but the content fits early November 1942 (at Norfolk after the Nov. 1 letter, leaving next morning for Solomons). The '1943' and the 'Z 43' filename appear to be mistaken. A second scan (Adobe 421209pg1) shows '1943' struck through and a later annotation '? 12/9/42'. Dec. 9, 1942 was a Wednesday, but by 12/8/42 Tom was already aboard ship after Solomons, so early November 1942 (after the 11/1 Norfolk letter, before the 11/14 Solomons envelope) remains the best fit.
other_dates_mentioned: to-morrow morning - departure for Solomons Island, MD
letters.location: Naval Operating Base, Norfolk, Virginia
letters.notes: Tom is leaving Norfolk for Solomons Island. The C.O. ordered young officers on 2-hour night hikes to keep them out of the officers' club bar. Lodging cost 25 cents a night and meals 20-30 cents. Chet's friend offered a job moving aviation gasoline from storage tanks to planes; Tom declined, saying 'they want an engineer not a C.& F.'er' (C&F probably means Commerce & Finance, likely his college degree at Penn State).

letters.date_source: written as 'Friday'. A later annotation '? 12/18/42' (and the filename) is contradicted by the content: this is Tom's arrival letter at Solomons, the day after leaving Norfolk (see the 'Wednesday' Norfolk letter, 1942-11-04), and by 12/8/42 he had already left Solomons.
other_dates_mentioned: yesterday (Thursday, about Nov. 5, 1942) - 12-hour trip from Norfolk
letters.location: U.S. Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (just arrived)
letters.notes: Tom arrived at Solomons after a 12-hour boat trip from Norfolk, sleeping on camp stools among 200 men. 25 officers were quartered on cots in a club room. He admires the 'barges' (landing craft) at the dock. New address: U.S. Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland. He asks Mother to send clothes (not blues or whites) and the sweater and socks from Mrs. Mortimer.

letters.date_source: written as 'Monday'. A later annotation '? 12/21/42' (and the filename) conflicts with the content, which fits Tom's first week at Solomons (navigation classes starting; compare the 1942-11-18 letter: 'last week I started in Elementary Navigation which was too elementary'). Tom had left Solomons by Dec. 8, 1942.
other_dates_mentioned: last night (Sunday) - evening in 'the city' (Solomons town)
letters.location: U.S. Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland
letters.notes: A WWI-veteran lieutenant tells tall tales; men bought hunting knives after being told they were 'commandos'. Tom describes the local bar behind the hotel, with slot machines and a Black pianist (described with a racial slur, transcribed as written for historical accuracy). His crew of ten lost its senior officer, and Tom led it on a hike. Navigation classes started at an elementary level even though the men had just finished a 3-month course. A second scan (misfiled as 430130) shows the signature 'Tom'.

letters.written_to: Dad (Mr. John A. Beck, Karns City, Penna.)
letters.location: U.S. Naval Amphibious Training Base (U.S.N.A.T.B.), Solomons Branch (Solomons, Maryland; mail routed via Washington, D.C.)
letters.notes: ENVELOPE ONLY. It confirms Tom's rank as Ensign by November 1942, his posting to the Naval Amphibious Training Base at Solomons, Maryland, and his father's name, Mr. John A. Beck of Karns City, Pa. The abbreviation before 'F. Beck' is probably 'Thos.' (Thomas). The letter it held may be the undated 'Wednesday' letter to Dad of 1942-11-18 or another November letter.

letters.date_source: written on letter ('Nov, 1942 Sunday'); '11/16/42?' was added later by another hand
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (inferred: the LCT training in 'the bay' is Chesapeake Bay, and Fish Point is nearby)
letters.notes: A vivid, story-like account of Tom's first night ship-handling on an LCT (Landing Craft, Tank, about 105 ft), with dialogue with the gruff skipper: taking the con, a near-collision, rules on the 'burdened vessel', and a missed 'meet her' turn. He explains the LCT engine controls, which work 'just like John's boat'. He promises to tell next time 'how this same skipper pulled a fast one on us'. '5C' is written at top left, perhaps an archivist's mark.

letters.date_source: written on letter as 'Wednesday 1942', with '? 11/18/42' added later. Nov. 18, 1942 was a Wednesday. The filename '420716' is misleading.
other_dates_mentioned: Saturday (probably Nov. 21, 1942) - possible leave from 5 to 10 to see Betty & John
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (written on leftover Midshipmen's School stationery)
letters.notes: By now Tom is a commissioned officer in the new Amphibious Force. He has a temporary crew, which he musters and marches to class and mess. His classes are Elementary Navigation and Communications (blinker, semaphore, ciphers). He explains the landing craft types LCT, LCI, and LST, and says he has been assigned to an LST but the harbor is too small for them (he later served on LCI(L) 62). He criticizes Navy red tape and politicians. Scuttlebutt says the base is moving to the West Coast. 'The Yanks are doing allright in Africa' refers to Operation Torch (landings on Nov. 8, 1942). He mentions Betty & John, who were apparently near Washington, D.C. (possibly his sister and her husband; a 1943 photo in the 'Tom Beck' folder is titled 'Tom and Betty ca 1943'). Dad had been ill and is feeling better. 421118PG1.jpg is a second scan of page 1 filed under the correct date; the 420716 filenames are misdated.

letters.date_source: written on letter as 'Friday 1942'; '? 11/20/42' was added later
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (on leftover Midshipmen's School stationery)
letters.notes: Dad had been ill (Mother's letter gave Tom 'quite a jolt'). Tom urges him to retire or semi-retire. Officers leave on 24 hours' notice by the 0600 boat. Tom was replaced as crew officer by a gunnery officer and given crew number 4074, which has no men yet. Eight men share his room, five of them from John Jay Hall. He lost $2 at blackjack.

letters.date_source: the letter says 'Sunday 1943', but the content fits Sunday, Nov. 22, 1942 (the day after Betty & John's visit planned in the 1942-11-18 letter, and before the Monday embarkation mentioned 1942-11-24). The '1943' appears to be a mistaken later annotation. A second scan (Adobe 421213pg1) shows '1943' struck through and a later annotation '? 12/13/42'; but the 12/8/42 letter shows Tom had already left Solomons, so Nov. 22 remains the best fit.
other_dates_mentioned: last night / Saturday (Nov. 21, 1942) - visit from Betty & John
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland
letters.notes: KEY: Tom has been transferred to an LCI (158 ft) crew of 3 officers and 21 men, as EXECUTIVE OFFICER, in charge until a skipper arrives. Betty and 'the Johns' visited; Tom regrets being in a bad mood because he couldn't get leave. This is the same visit described in the undated 'Sunday' letter to 'Sis' (Undated D), so Sis = Betty, and that letter was probably written the same day. Future mail goes c/o Post Office, New York.

letters.date_source: undated ('Sunday'); matched by content to the 1942-11-22 letter to Dad, which describes the same Saturday visit by Betty and Tom's bad mood
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (inferred)
letters.notes: Marked '(over)', but the back was not scanned. Tom apologizes for being in a bad humor during the visit and for the bad impression he gave of the base. 'Tell the kid I said hello' may refer to Betty's child, or to a younger sibling or a nephew (possibly 'Hickory', mentioned 1942-09-19).

letters.date_source: written as 'Nov. 1942, Tuesday'; exact day from filename, consistent with the 'Happy Thanksgiving' closing
other_dates_mentioned: Christmas / New Year's - split holiday leave
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (inferred)
letters.notes: The base is muddy. Tom bought galoshes for the steel decks. His scheduled embarkation was cancelled, and seven of his crew were taken away. Holiday leave will be split between Christmas and New Year's. His friend Chet is eager to get his own ship. Men who flunk out of John Jay now stay in as Seamen 2nd class.

letters.date_source: written on letter ('Thanksgiving'); Thanksgiving 1942 was Nov. 26
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (inferred)
letters.notes: Thanksgiving: Tom's roommate and buddy Baker jumped for a departing 105-ft boat and fell in the water. Tom did helmsman and man-overboard (box) drills. He complains about how the enlisted men are treated (no liberty or pay, no clothes) and about the base staff's easy hours. He mentions a Butler (PA) hospital holding a dance. Dad had been writing daily. The letter contains antisemitic remarks, echoing Dad's comments about 'soft jobs'; they are transcribed as written for historical accuracy, and a content note is included in the transcription.

letters.date_source: written as 'Saturday night, Nov 1942'; exact day from filename (Nov. 28, 1942 was a Saturday)
other_dates_mentioned: Nov. 30 (1942) issue of Time magazine, page 70 (for John)
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (inferred)
letters.notes: Assembled from both folders: pages 2 and 4 exist only in the parent folder (4211AB...). Tom explains LCI crew organization (C.O. as navigator, Exec as gunnery/damage control/supply officer, engineering officer; 3 officers and 21 men). His crew so far is one officer and 14 men. A veteran gunner's mate (Pearl Harbor, Midway, Solomons) dodged an instructor interview to stay with Tom's crew but was sent to an LST anyway. Tom says an officer must also be a 'Mother' to young sailors. Roommates: Coopersmith (Chicago) and Baker (Missouri, Yale M.A. in English, former teacher and reporter). A margin note asks John to read page 70 of the Nov. 30 Time. It contains an antisemitic remark about Coopersmith, transcribed as written.

original_files: TBF1 Navy Letters/Z 42 11 AE Pg 2 A.jpg
letters.date_source: written on letter ('Wednesday NOV 1942'); the filenames '42062x' (June 1942) and '421118' are unreliable
other_dates_mentioned: Dec. 25 (1942) - rumored commissioning date of Tom's ship
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (inferred; on leftover Midshipmen's School stationery)
letters.notes: Page 2 was found in 421118 pG1.jpg; the old 'Z 42 11 AE' pair confirms the two pages belong together. Tom's crew was assigned a commanding officer and seven more men. The ship is rumored to be commissioned Dec. 25 at New Orleans or another Gulf port, which fits Tom being in Texas in January 1943. Most staff jobs are going to married men. His friend Chet has another type of ship and expects to leave soon; they hope to meet during 'maneuvers in the Gulf'. Contains antisemitic and anti-Japanese remarks, transcribed as written.

other_dates_mentioned: 'One moon ago' (about Nov. 5, 1942) - arrival at Solomons
letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland
letters.notes: Evening classes cut into Tom's letter-writing time. He received gifts from his parents, from Hank & Harriet (socks), and from the Woman's Missionary Society (probably the family's church). He is in his third week of communications training. He marks one month since arriving at Solomons, which is consistent with the early-November Norfolk letter. The parent-folder file 421203pg1.jpg is misnamed; it is page 1 of the 12/8/42 letter.

letters.location: Naval Amphibious Training Base, Solomons, Maryland (leaving next day)
letters.notes: KEY: Tom's crew 3081 leaves Solomons the next morning for USS LCI(L) #218 (a temporary training ship; the address will last about two weeks). This explains the '#218' mail mentioned in the 1943-01-18 letter. The crew is at 2/3 strength in men, and Tom is the only one of three officers, and the crew's censor. A strict all-day muster was held at the base.

letters.location: Aboard ship / new post (not named; 'no seasickness yet' suggests he is now aboard)
letters.notes: Tom left Solomons on short notice and is now organizing his crew and making out a watch bill and working parties. He has no seasickness yet. Written on plain lined paper because he had no stationery. Gifts: cookies from Florella (reading uncertain) and candy from Aunt Hazel. He writes thank-you letters to the Red Cross for clothing Mrs. Mortimer gave him, spacing them out so the volunteers think he received the items at his post, to keep their morale up.

letters.location: Aboard ship (not named), anchored overnight
letters.notes: Tom is aboard ship in rough water: most of the crew were seasick, but he wasn't. He hopes for shore leave to get his first haircut since being home. Everyone sleeps in their clothes, taking off only shoes and cap, and he got hot water from the cook to shave. The parent folder holds duplicate scans (including 421210pg2A).

other_dates_mentioned: Saturday & Sunday nights (Dec. 12-13, 1942) - movies in Norfolk
letters.location: Aboard ship at anchor near Norfolk, Virginia (having left Solomons)
letters.notes: This is the first letter on the ship's-wheel 'UNITED STATES NAVY' stationery. Tom mentions censorship: they can write about little besides their health. The ship is at anchor near Norfolk with little to do. He saw 'Road to Morocco' and 'White Cargo' in Norfolk and jokes that Solomons' movie films were 15 years old. Rumors of Christmas leave or a few weeks of training elsewhere. He hasn't bathed since leaving Solomons. He asks someone to buy Janny a Christmas gift.

letters.location: Aboard a ship for the night, en route to Portsmouth (probably Portsmouth, Virginia)
letters.notes: Tom returned a little late from Christmas leave at home, riding down from Washington with men from another training crew. He will meet his crew at Portsmouth; they left on the 22nd. He spent the night in the C.O.'s bed aboard a ship. The warm weather is 'like Spring'.

letters.location: Portsmouth (probably Portsmouth, Virginia; a Virginia railway station and a 'true Virginian' are mentioned)
letters.notes: Tom rejoined his crew, now at full strength, which needs only officers. Crew number 3081 should go on all letters. Friends Baker and Toben (reading uncertain) left for their ship. Tom will leave soon but 'not going into the heart of it'. He had an hour-long conversation with an 84-year-old Virginian woman who claimed descent from Patrick Henry. The letter contains period ethnic slurs, transcribed as written.

letters.location: Portsmouth, Virginia (Navy Yard, i.e. Norfolk Navy Yard at Portsmouth), leaving that night for Houston, Texas
letters.notes: The crew is leaving by train for Houston. The other two officers arrived and left the same day, and Tom rides with the crew. He spent a dull New Year's Eve at the Navy Yard officers' club and calls it 'the most unfriendly town I have been in'. His pay account was closed before he was paid, so he may wire home for money (he did; see 1943-01-05). He asks Mother to get his white suit and shoes ready to ship. Christmas mail came from Bill Jamison (there is a 'Z Bill Jameson' letter in the collection) and from 'Luke & Lena' (see 1943-01-24).

letters.location: Houston, Texas (on Rice Hotel stationery); a small Navy base nearby
letters.notes: The train arrived in Houston 10 hours late after a 10-hour layover in New Orleans, where Tom had trouble rounding up his sailors. He reports to the base on Jan. 7. He wired home for money because his pay account was closed. Texas had no bars (liquor was sold by the bottle only), so he'll 'stick to beer'. This explains the 'Texas' references in the Jan. 18 letter and the 'new address' in the Jan. 8 letter.

letters.location: Navy base 18 miles outside Houston, Texas
letters.notes: Now complete: page 1 is in the Adobe folder and page 2 in TBF0defective. Tom reported to the base on Jan. 7 and is doing paperwork for equipping the ship, expecting about 2 more weeks there. He stays on base to save money. He bought another khaki uniform and asks Mother to forget the whites because it is cold and rainy.

other_dates_mentioned: Saturday night (Jan. 9, 1943) - town full of servicemen
letters.location: Houston, Texas
letters.notes: Letters came from Mother and from George (possibly the 'Geo.' of the 'ZGeoAllegheny' letters). Houston is full of air cadets from Ellington Field. Tom slept at the YMCA in a friend's bed, and is dating a girl named Ophelia (the girl mentioned in the 1943-01-18 letter). A former C.O. from Solomons, met at Paradise Creek (Portsmouth, VA), has a brother-in-law in Houston who invited Tom to dinner. He expects to go to Galveston for a while. A new crew member who served in Africa mentioned an officer Glenn Scott, likely the one from Oil City, PA (Glenn Scott also appears in the 1942-07-08 letter as Officer of the Deck at Columbia). Tom warns that another telegram asking for money may come.

letters.date_source: the letter reads '1/15/42', a New Year slip; a later annotation reads '1/15/43?'. The content confirms 1943.
other_dates_mentioned: Wednesday (Jan. 13, 1943) - dinner with a Houston family
next Wednesday (Jan. 20, 1943) - invited back, basketball game
letters.location: Houston, Texas (ship being outfitted; Galveston next)
letters.notes: Tom expects to sail for the PACIFIC in a few months, and mail will go via a Postmaster address once they reach Galveston. The skipper 'knows less about the ship than I do'. The ship is full of workmen, so there is little to do. A staff Lt. gave a pep talk; he was the officer whose ship, anchored in a fairway at Little Creek, was hit by the Cape Charles Ferry. Tom jokes about the 'Ambiguous Force' (Amphibious Force) being 'Snafu'. Income tax details: pay of $21 as Apprentice Seaman, $195 as Midshipman, $300 as Ensign, plus a $150 uniform gratuity, and income from a 'Co. trust' and Agency account; John should pay the tax. Also mentions Sprecher (Pittsburgh address possibly 5 Highland Court), Chet's wedding, and looking up the McMahons and O'Conners.

other_dates_mentioned: last Saturday/Sunday (Jan. 16-17, 1943) - warm sun, then a 'Norther'
letters.location: Houston, Texas
letters.notes: Complete with page 2 from the Adobe folder. Tom suspects they are headed 'to the southwest' (the Pacific) via California, with a month of Gulf maneuvers first, and suggests Mother change a planned Florida trip to a California trip to see him. He explains the money he wired for (uniform, sunglasses, loans to unpaid men, pricey hotels). Mentions 'the girl I met here' (Ophelia, per 1943-01-11), Sprecher's letter, mail sent to his December 1942 training ship USS LCI(L) #218 (see 1942-12-05), and the Texas weather.

letters.location: Houston, Texas, aboard the newly commissioned USS LCI(L) 345 (leaving for Galveston)
letters.notes: KEY: Tom's ship was commissioned Friday, Jan. 22, 1943, and leaves for Galveston the next day. The '#345' written into the address refers to USS LCI(L) 345; the 1943-01-26 letter gives the address 'USS LCI(L) 345, Postmaster N.Y., N.Y.'. (Tom was transferred to another ship around Jan. 31, 1943, and was aboard LCI(L) 62 by March.) Gifts: tobacco and a pipe from John Mc., washcloths from Luke & Lena (which clarifies 'Luke & Lines' in the 1943-01-02 letter), and mittens from John B. Letters from Uncle Paul and Adam. John wrote about a lease with 'so many partners' (possibly an oil or gas lease on family property). Tom will start sending a pay allotment home. He mentions Jimmy Eisler (reading uncertain) in Galveston and the McMahons and O'Connors in Houston.

letters.location: Aboard USS LCI(L) 345 (Galveston, Texas area)
letters.notes: KEY: this letter names Tom's first ship, USS LCI(L) 345 (commissioned Jan. 22, 1943), with the mailing address 'USS LCI(L) 345, Postmaster N.Y., N.Y.'. Tom is busy with shipboard routine. He again asks for his whites and shoes and says airmail is no faster.

letters.location: Aboard USS LCI(L) 345 (Galveston, Texas area)
letters.notes: Tom bluffs about oil when the Engineering Officer asks him questions, which may be a hint of a pre-war oil-industry background (compare the 'lease' in 1943-01-24). He wishes Isabel a happy birthday and admits forgetting Jackie's. Address: USS L.C.I.(L) 345, c/o Postmaster, New York, N.Y.

letters.location: Aboard USS LCI(L) 345 (Galveston/Houston, Texas area)
letters.notes: KEY: Tom is being transferred from LCI(L) 345 to replace the sick executive officer of LCI(L) 62 ('The other ship is #62'), where he is found in the 1943-03-12 letter. He received a letter from Margorie, who plays basketball (probably his sister), and hard candy from Bertha Beck (a relative). He mentions the Roudybush wedding in Houston (reading uncertain). His pay came to $366 by check, and he plans to send a money order home. Now complete: page 2 is in the Adobe folder.

letters.location: Aboard USS LCI(L) 62 (Gulf coast, Texas; newly transferred)
letters.notes: KEY: Tom's transfer took effect that evening, from LCI(L) 345 to LCI(L) 62 (named in the 1943-01-31 letter) as executive officer. The new skipper is a full Lieutenant. Tom reflects on quietly working around his old skipper, who refused advice. He encloses two money orders and leaves John to decide what to do with them. George has started a new semester at school (George appears to be a younger brother or relative in college).

letters.location: At anchor in a hot foreign port after first ocean voyage aboard LCI(L) 62 (location not named, censored; 'the coldest month of the year' but hot, so probably the Caribbean or Panama)
letters.notes: This is Tom's first letter after going to sea. He boarded LCI(L) 62 the night before sailing and stood the 12-to-4 watches, his first time running a ship on the open sea at night, in a darkened ship. He did most of the celestial navigation without having taken a sextant sight before, and the skipper thought his positions were more accurate than the lead ship's. He is now at anchor, having left the U.S. ('if & when I get back to the states'). He plans to use V-mail. Mail sent to the 345 should still catch up with him.

letters.location: Foreign port (not named, censored), aboard LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Tom's first night ashore in a foreign port: a 'quaint' town where almost every other door is a jammed bar. After the ocean trip he has more confidence that the LCIs 'can take quite a bit of punishment'. He will send letters by Air Mail or V-mail. Censorship limits what he can write.

letters.location: Foreign port (not named), aboard LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Typewritten. Gives the full name of Tom's friend Chet: Chet BEARD. Chet married while waiting for his ship in Philadelphia, and he and Tom met up in the same foreign port. Johnson and other 'John Jay boys' came with Chet. Tom asks about Jackie ('getting cuter and wilder', probably a young child in the family) and fuel oil rationing at home, and mentions the story of Al Wiengard leaving. The signature falls below the edge of the scan.

other_dates_mentioned: One week from to-day (Feb. 27, 1943) - TOM'S BIRTHDAY
letters.location: Foreign port (not named), aboard LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: KEY FAMILY DETAILS: Tom's birthday is Feb. 27 ('One week from to-day...'), and he jokes about getting 'up in years' for 'a young man's war'. He asks about the family: Isabel (at home, in Butler, or joining the WAVES/WAACs?), Janny (in school, 'getting along without Bill', probably Janny's husband or boyfriend in service), John Mc. (new job), John B. (still single), George (working hard, in school), and Marg (Margorie, playing basketball). Mother collects old silk (for the war effort) and serves on the rationing board. He has a new mailing address (not included in this scan).

letters.location: Foreign port (not named), aboard LCI(L) 62, about to put to sea
letters.notes: This may be the last letter 'for awhile' because the ship is going to sea again. Tom wishes he had seen the West Coast before leaving the States, which suggests the ship is heading into the Pacific without stopping in California (consistent with transiting the Panama Canal). The address changes to whatever is on the envelope; don't use 'Amphibious Force'. The cook is a good baker.

letters.location: Anchored in a foreign port (not named), aboard LCI(L) 62, departing next morning
letters.notes: This is the last letter before a long ocean passage: 'Don't worry if you don't hear from me for a couple of months.' Crew members are clipping or shaving their heads, and Tom plans to clip the skipper when they cross the equator. This matches the 1943-03-12 letter, in which Tom has shaved his head and crossed the Equator, so the ship crossed into the South Pacific in early March 1943. Tom is reading Balzac, which John lent or recommended.

letters.date_source: typed on letter ('USS LCI(L) 62, March 12, 1943'), with continuations dated Mar. 15, 3/16, and 3/18
other_dates_mentioned: 'a few days ago' (early March 1943) - crossed the Equator
letters.location: At sea aboard USS LCI(L) 62 in the South Pacific, approaching port after crossing the Equator
letters.notes: Mostly TYPEWRITTEN; finished by hand on 3/18 because someone else was using the typewriter. Now complete with page 2 from the Adobe folder. Tom became a 'shellback' (he writes 'moss-back') in King Neptune's Court when crossing the Equator at night, clipped his head and grew a beard, took noon sun sights, and stood 4-on/8-off watches. They passed an island with mountains, then a two-day storm in the rainy season. He worries about his income tax (the government owes him about $200) and washes clothes in salt water. He hopes to come back 'as a passenger'. Heavily stained; a later hand added 'MARCH 1943' in blue.

letters.location: A South Pacific port with a post office (not named), aboard LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Typewritten. The ship is in port after another leg, standing 4-on/4-off watches. They expect to reach their destination within a month. Beer is rationed first-come, first-served. The Captain sent Tom ashore for provisions. Tom hopes for leave in the States in 3-4 months. AirMail reaches the States in about 10 days.

letters.written_to: 'Unc' (an uncle; not named, possibly Uncle Paul mentioned 1943-01-24)
other_dates_mentioned: about six weeks ago (late February 1943) - left the States
last of January (1943) - original ship commissioned
letters.location: Anchored in the bay of a 'fair sized city' in the South Pacific (not named, censored), aboard LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: A retrospective letter to an uncle: Tom was transferred from his original ship because another ship lost an officer, and they left the States the next day. The voyage is in about five legs ('long, damn long, and the rest rather short'). He handled the ship in a harbor for the first time when the anchor slipped in a storm. At one dry outpost he tried native banana brew. He grew a six-week black beard over a blond buzz cut, then shaved because of his helmet chin strap. He has heard nothing from home since January. He says leaving Mother was 'the toughest day I have had' and that she has many of her family near her, so this uncle is likely on Mother's side.

letters.written_to: Mother (Mrs John A Beck, Karns City, Penn.)
letters.location: Sent by cable from the South Pacific ('VIA IMP', routing not identified); received via the telegraph office at a Butler, PA hotel
letters.notes: An 11-word cablegram: 'ALL WELL AND SAFE PLEASE DONT WORRY LOVE KISSES - THOS BECK'. It was telephoned to Mrs. Beck. Tom mentions sending it in the 1943-04-13 V-mail and worries that it might have scared her.

letters.written_to: Mother (Mrs. John A. Beck, Karns City, Pennsylvania)
letters.location: South Pacific port (not named), aboard USS LCI(L) 62; mail via Fleet Post Office San Francisco
letters.notes: This is a V-MAIL (microfilmed and reduced) form, No. 1116, passed by the Naval Censor. Return address: 'Ens. Thos. F. Beck, USS LCI(L) 62, c/o P.M. San Francisco, Cal.' Tom sent a cablegram (1943-04-12) and hopes it didn't scare her. He wrote to Uncle Chauncey, Betty, and Luke, and plans letters to '711 E. Pearl' (an address, perhaps relatives in Butler), Adam, The Becks, Mari, and Sally. He sent $200 home from Galveston. He typed this in the radio room while listening to war news, sports (baseball season), and a waltz.

other_dates_mentioned: Yesterday (April 14, 1943) - first Mail Call since leaving the States
letters.location: South Pacific port (not named), aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: A long reply written after the first mail call since leaving the States (35-40 letters and 4 packages). The paper is embossed with the ship's seal 'DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY - U.S.S. LCI(L)-62', and Tom asks 'What do you think of our ship's seal?'. INCOMPLETE: the backs of sheets '-2-' and '-3-' were not scanned (pages 3-4 and 5-6 are duplicate pairs), so two passages are missing. RICH FAMILY DETAILS: Izzy (Isabel) may become a teacher; George's grades and draft decision (Tom advises him not to rush; service life is 'tough and abnormal'); Bill J. (Jamison?) and Dick B. (an aviation cadet); Don W. (regular Navy, high rating) and Geo. W.; Tom is on the 'honor roll at the office' of his pre-war employer; Harriet's expected baby; Mary Jane as a mother; Betty expecting ('U. Paul's chest' will puff up, so Uncle Paul would be the grandfather: Betty may be Uncle Paul's daughter, i.e. Tom's cousin rather than sister); 'the cherub' is a grandson in Butler (Betty's son?); Lucy McClung's marriage; Mrs. McClung and Betty's apartment; a dream road trip on the new Alaska Highway; Mother as 'Pres. of Beck, Inc.'; John and Fran possibly engaged ('Fran will need a bridesmaid'). The whites and shoes arrived but aren't needed.

letters.location: South Pacific port (not named), aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Page 2 was found in the Adobe folder; a short passage between the pages may be missing (see the file header). Tom censors the crew's mail and jokes about his spelling. They received a coxswain(?) by transfer who has been in the Naval Reserves 15 years and 'knows his Navy'. Tom spends long hours standing in the conning tower. Written on thin Air Mail paper. The two TBF0defective images are duplicate scans of page 1.

letters.date_source: written on letter ('April 25, 1943'); Easter Sunday 1943 was April 25, which confirms it
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62 (warm climate)
letters.notes: Now complete with page 4 from the Adobe folder. Easter turkey dinner with Ritz-cracker stuffing, losing track of days, disillusionment with foreign travel ('See America First'), radio news, and packing away winter gear from Little Creek. He is borrowing John's bag. The P.S. asks whether it is 'safe now to send John around to check up on a few things at 316 Second Street' (a Tom-related address, unexplained). 'Air-mail is the best service out here.'

letters.written_to: Mother (Mrs. John A. Beck, Karns City, Pennsylvania)
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62 (via Postmaster San Francisco)
letters.notes: V-MAIL, typed, passed by the Naval Censor. No mail from home since the big April 14 mail call; the last letter was from Aunt Harriet. Experienced Navy transfers have eased Tom's deck supervision. He is acting as ship's Yeoman while the Radioman/Yeoman is away. He looks up every destroyer hoping to find Don (Izzy's connection; Don W. in the regular Navy, 1943-04-15), whom Izzy may be linked to romantically. Typed Morse-like marks at lower left may be a coded sign-off.

other_dates_mentioned: April 7 (1943) - Mother's letter posted in Petrolia
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Tom has a heavy load censoring the crew's mail. Night school in Navigation has started; he credits his six weeks at Pitt (University of Pittsburgh), three months at John Jay, and two months of practical work. He sent a money order from Galveston and a cablegram. He regrets being unable to send a Mother's Day gift. A V-mail from Aunt Lyle took about a month to reach him; 'K.C.' is Karns City. Mother's letter was posted in Petrolia, PA (near Karns City). The last line of pg1 and the signature are cut off in the scans.

letters.date_source: written as 'Sunday May 9'; year added later. May 9, 1943 was a Sunday and was Mother's Day.
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Written on Mother's Day (without saying so): Tom is homesick and thinking of home. The crew had an afternoon of recreation on the beach with beer, football, and softball. The Captain was sick for a few days, so Tom and the Engineering Officer ran the ship.

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: IMPORTANT FAMILY CLUE: Mother gave books to the school in Tom's name, and Tom asks 'What picture of Dad are they going to use in the school-house?', which suggests a memorial to Dad. Together with Dad's illness in Nov. 1942, Tom's Christmas 1942 leave home, letters from Feb. 1943 on addressed only to Mother, Tom calling leaving Mother 'the toughest day I have had' (1943-04-07), and 'puffs up like Dad did' (past tense, 1943-04-15), this strongly suggests Tom's father, John A. Beck, died around December 1942 or January 1943 (not stated outright in these letters; worth verifying). Other items: George chose Navy V-12 (Tom mistakenly thinks it's the WAVES); Dick is in sick bay rooming with Armstrong (Tom's Penn State friend) and may be assigned to Slippery Rock; the family cottage (probably 'the Lake'); Henry is on the African front; winter clothing may be sent home. He likes Zane Grey, Thorne Smith, and Balzac. P.S. to Jackie.

other_dates_mentioned: around the 27th of May - Marge's birthday
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: The bottom line of pages 1-3 is cut off in all scans. FAMILY: John (Tom's brother) is engaged ('if he waits for me it will be a long engagement'; the 1943-04-15 letter hints Fran is the bride). Uncle John 'finally gave in' to Libby, and Libby may be going back with Buddy. Marge (Margorie) is becoming a young lady, with her birthday around May 27. Henry is on the African front ('Africa is just about de-loused', the Tunisia campaign ended May 13, 1943). Tom is shipping his woolens, raincoat, and whites home in a mailing case and John's suitcase. An uncashable check is mentioned, but a later note says he can't find it. He describes a Navy officer's cap device he bought.

letters.location: South Pacific port, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Tom found the missing check (see 1943-05-16) and enclosed it. While taking the crew's excess clothing ashore for storage, he dropped the Captain's box overboard, then kept away at the Club until the Captain cooled off. Mother is having her eyes checked at a clinic; Betty reports Mother's health is excellent. Marge is writing about dances.

letters.location: A new South Pacific port (arrived at dark after another voyage), aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: The ship has moved to a new port. Tom still stands the 12-4 watches. He forgot to return Uncle Frank's gun before leaving home (the bolt should be in the front bedroom) and jokes he might get him a 'Jap rifle' in return. Mail will take weeks to catch up.

letters.location: South Pacific port (coconut trees), aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: INCOMPLETE: ends mid-sentence after page 2. Tom received Mother's letters with Jackie's pictures, Henry's letter, and John's engagement announcement, and read them 'sitting under a coconut tree drinking beer'. He wrote to Henry (on the Africa front). John's wedding is coming, and Tom can't attend. Also mentions spring rain delaying the gardens at home and good Allied war news.

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: There is a gap in the collection between June 11 and Aug. 1, 1943 (the period of the New Georgia campaign in the Solomons, where LCIs were heavily used; not mentioned in the letters because of censorship). George has joined the Navy. John has married; he got 'Stephens furniture' and possibly the house. Tom had a headache from too much sun. Rumors say they may get home soon. A page may be missing between pg1 and pg2a, and the left edge of pg2a is cut off.

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Tom lists the photos he carries: Libby's wedding, 'the kid' (4), Mother (2), the kids and the magnolia (6), Luke & Lena, Luke, and Mari. He asks for more photos, especially a better one of Mother. Isabel apparently joined the Navy (WAVES, 'An Old Sea B') and made a remark about insignia. 'The Boot' (George, in boot training) wrote from Lewisburg, PA (the V-12 program at Bucknell University). A clipping about the parties for John & Fran's wedding featured Mrs. J. H. McClung Jr. (possibly Betty, if she married a McClung). He mentions Jackie wrecking the house.

other_dates_mentioned: about five days ago (about Aug. 19, 1943) - mail received
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Mother sent Ernie Pyle's articles about the LCIs ('sea going barges'), and Tom notes the LCIs were mentioned in Time. Also: a stag party (for John's wedding), 'I am sorry about Nunks', Tucker joining the Navy, Glenn Scott's new assignment on a big ship, and Geo. Wagenhorst turns out to be working nearby. Sally received her ring (engaged to Johnny, who is leaving soon). Tom has two months' pay on the books and an uncollected Norfolk-to-Houston travel allowance of about $100. He is ready 'for a soft berth'. A pencil '383' mark appears across pg3.

other_dates_mentioned: August 1943 - John & Fran's wedding ('getting a daughter') and Mother's birthday
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62 ('living off the Army' for rations)
letters.notes: KEY FAMILY: John married Fran in August 1943 (Mother 'getting a daughter'), and Mother had her birthday in August (Tom jokes 'life begins at 40' teasingly). Janny caught Bill ('My best wishes to the conqueror'), so Janny and Bill are engaged or married. Mac wrote and offered tobacco; Tom asks for pipes instead. 'Old money bags' and 'financial wizard' refer to John, Tom's financial adviser. 'The new Beck family' means John and Fran. Joe is a shipmate. Plink [?] asks about Tom. As pay officer, Tom carried $1,685 to pay the crew; he left $540 on the books for a 30-day leave next year and some for Mari. The enclosed check is the Norfolk-Houston travel allowance. He cut open his shoes for the heat. Izzy is 'hunting' (romantically).

other_dates_mentioned: the day after to-morrow (Sept. 7, 1943) - school starts again at home
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: A quiet Sunday with Tom reading a book. A 'movie boat' visits. War news: the Allies have landed in Europe (Italy, Sept. 3, 1943), and the Japanese are retreating island by island ('mass cross-island run to Tokyo'). School starts at home in two days, and Mother's garden harvest and canning are coming. 'Pardon the envelope' suggests something unusual about the envelope, which was not scanned. The letter contains wartime slurs, transcribed as written.

other_dates_mentioned: Last evening (Sept. 8, 1943) - visit from Geo. W.
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62 (part of an LCI Flotilla)
letters.notes: Geo. W. (George Wagenhorst, from Columbia/John Jay) visited Tom aboard ship; the only officer Tom knows 'outside of the Flotilla'. Geo. W. asked about Isabel. A movie had a broken sound machine. Italy's surrender (announced Sept. 8, 1943) and progress in New Guinea lifted spirits. A trainee officer, Jim Hoffman of Cleveland, came aboard. Florella wrote about wedding pictures.

other_dates_mentioned: first of the year (1944) - possible relief
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: The recipient is almost certainly Mother despite the 'Hiya Sweetheart' greeting: it references her recent birthday party ('Don't start grabbing for a cane') and her vacation, matching the 1943-08-31 letter, and invites her to keep house for him near a stateside shipyard ('the life of a Navy wife'). Mother vacationed at Ocean City and is considering Butler or Florida for the winter. Plans for the crew's relief have been dropped until about the first of the year; relieved men usually go to new construction (as Don W. is doing now). Geo. W. suggested a party with Isabel and 'the Dick Becks' (so Dick Beck is a relative, perhaps the Dick of the Dick & Betty wedding, 1942-07-18).

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Some mail was lost. Tom asks for leather slippers, size 10 1/2, as a Christmas gift. An Army show was put on for the men. He had his first ice cream in a long time at the canteen. He received a letter from Marge's friend Thos. Lipinski.

other_dates_mentioned: the 24th (Sept. 24, 1943) - Mother's letter with farming pictures
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Mother sent 'farming pictures'; Tom's only other photo of her was taken waiting for a streetcar at Canonsburg (PA). He mentions Aunt Bess, a party at the Moshers' (compare the Adam Moser letter of 1942-07-15; 'Adam & Dorothy' may be the Mosers), and says 'John & George inherited their poker sense from Dad, I got mine from you', which confirms that John and George are Tom's BROTHERS. Shipmates Schwalbach and Hofmann (Jim Hoffman/Hofmann, the trainee from Cleveland) play Sheepshead with him. Aunt Harriet is looking for a wife for Tom. A check will be sent home soon.

letters.written_to: John & Fran (Tom's brother and new sister-in-law)
letters.date_source: written on letter ('Oct. 9-43'); the filename 431008 is a day off
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Tom thanks John & Fran for the first wedding photo and brags about his 'beautiful sister-in-law'. The couple fixed up a house; John is building a coal cellar ('pessimistic about the oil future', which suggests John worked in the oil business). They made a trip to New York (races) and to a convention. Shipboard breakfast is powdered eggs or pancakes ('collision mats'). There is much scuttlebutt about the crew's relief.

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: A short note. There is a month-long gap after Oct. 9, 1943, which coincides with the Bougainville landings (Nov. 1, 1943) in the Solomons, where LCIs took part; not mentioned because of censorship. Tom received the first package (a book) but not the photos. Air Mail is delayed. He is 'short of time'.

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: Thanksgiving dinner of turkey, oyster stew, and cranberries, 'tho' not eaten under the best circumstances... There are many much worse off than I am'. There was a Bob Hope movie, and Tom joined a card 'game of skill' instead. He will request Ernie Pyle's book and write John about income tax. He wonders whether Mother spent Thanksgiving at Lewisburg (with George), Butler, or home.

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: A memorial was dedicated in Chicora, PA, probably across from Dick Gaisford's (compare the 1943-05-11 letter about Dad's picture for the school; possibly related to Dad). Tom hasn't seen 'white civilians' since leaving the States. Henry has moved from Africa to Italy, and Bill (Janny's) may be going across the Atlantic. Tom expects to finish 18 months in the Pacific, then serve Atlantic duty, then return. He dined with Glenn Scott on Scott's ship and accidentally told him about 'Jack' (apparently bad news the Scott family had withheld). MOTHER IS NOW A COMPANY DIRECTOR ('How do you like being a big director... did we make any money?'), probably of a family business with employees (compare 'Pres. of Beck, Inc.', 1943-04-15). Packages came from Frazier-McCafferty (a business?), Aunt Lyde, and Isabel, plus Mother's fruitcake and the slippers he requested. He wonders how he will have changed when he gets home.

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: A middle page is missing from all scans. Tom lists Christmas gifts from Florella, the Women's Missionary Society, Bertha & Carl, Luke & Lena, Geo., Janny, H. Ford(?), and the Pelkeys (see the 'Pelky' letters of 1943-12-25). KEY: 'When Dad's picture arrived I had such a strange sensation. I often think of him...' This further supports that Dad had died (see notes on 1943-05-11 and 1943-12-06). The old skipper has gone stateside; Tom may head stateside when his 18 months are up.

letters.written_to: Mrs. Brecht (wife of Reverend Brecht; for the Women's Missionary Society)
letters.location: Aboard U.S.S. LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: A formal thank-you for the Women's Missionary Society Christmas package. Reverend Brecht was presumably the pastor of the family's church (Karns City/Chicora area). Presumably the original was returned to or kept by the family.

letters.written_by: Tom (Ens. Thos. F. Beck); covering note by Olive (Pelkey)
letters.written_to: Olive & Bob (Pelkey); the covering note is to Elva (Tom's mother)
letters.date_source: written on letter ('25 Dec. 1943'); the covering note is dated 1/5/44
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62; the Pelkeys apparently lived in California ('a box of California fruits')
letters.notes: KEY: this gives TOM'S MOTHER'S FIRST NAME: ELVA ('Dear Elva: We are sending you Tommy's letter'), so she is Elva Beck (Mrs. John A. Beck). The 'Tom Beck' photo folder has a photo titled 'Elva w boys'. Tom's Christmas Day thank-you for the Pelkeys' fruitcake: turkey dinner, 'food that isn't dehydrated is really a rare treat'. Olive forwarded his letter to Elva, mentioning the flu, the Spitzers, and Dr. Mortimer (compare Mrs. Mortimer, who gave Tom clothing in 1942).

letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62
letters.notes: KEY: Tom will turn 25 ('a quarter of a century') at his next birthday; with his birthday of Feb. 27 (1943-02-20 letter), that means TOM WAS BORN FEB. 27, 1919. Betty's and Mincy's (reading uncertain) birthdays are both Jan. 5, 'another big day for the Becks', so Betty is apparently a Beck by birth (Tom's sister). Tom numbers his envelopes. Someone sends him Time magazine, and Aunt Bess sent 'Burma Surgeon' (he writes 'Burma Doctor'). Signed 'Love from An Old Man'.

other_dates_mentioned: in another week (Feb. 27, 1944) - 'another anniversary' (his birthday, and about a year overseas)
letters.location: South Pacific, aboard USS LCI(L) 62 - about to reach a liberty port, 'first for 12 months'
letters.notes: Geo. W. (Wagenhorst) has gone home and promised to visit Mother. Mother calculated when Tom could come home; he says it depends on the outfit, C.O., Flotilla Commander, and so on. His first liberty port in 12 months is coming. Central Pacific news is good (the Marshall Islands campaign, Feb. 1944). He has letters from Mari and Sally, and hopes 'Sally stays in Butler awhile' (a romantic interest?).

letters.location: Not stated; Tom is 'getting by with food and sleep' (possibly aboard a transport heading home - see 1944-04-04)
letters.notes: A short letter; Tom also wrote to John. Marjorie sent a sea-themed birthday present. He needs new slippers again. He is doing little besides eating and sleeping, which suggests he has left LCI(L) 62 and may be in transit. Next-day letter (1944-04-04) mentions Portsmouth and possible leave. The closing is cut off in the scan.

letters.location: Stateside shore duty - almost certainly Portland, Maine (175 State St. is a Portland address; see the 1945-03-15 letter from U.S. Naval Station, Grand Trunk Pier, Portland)
letters.notes: There is a gap in the collection from April to November 1944. Tom is now on shore duty and has moved to 175 State St. (telephone 3-0804), sharing with another officer. He received a Christmas package from the W.C.M.S. (Women's ... Missionary Society). He is 'still in the same status in regards to orders'. He felt relieved by news in letters from Mother and Isabel.

letters.written_to: Mother (Mrs. John A. Beck, Karns City, Pennsylvania)
other_dates_mentioned: first week in April (1945) - Mother's planned visit
letters.location: U.S. Naval Station, Grand Trunk Pier, Portland, Maine
letters.notes: Tom is stationed at U.S. Naval Station, Grand Trunk Pier, Portland, Maine, and is still an Ensign per the return address. Mother plans to visit the first week of April. His friend Lane (his 'entertainment committee') is being transferred. Tom expects changes (new orders) within a month or two. The McClungs are moving for a better position. George (brother, in the Navy) writes about liberty. His car license plate arrived.

letters.date_source: written as '4 April' with no year. Two scans exist, filed as 440404 and 450403. The content ('life of ease', afternoon walks 'around the yard', nightly movies, possible leave) matches Tom's stay at a naval hospital in April-May 1945 (see 1945-04-30 and 1945-05-08), so 1945 is the better fit.
letters.location: Probably U.S. Naval Hospital, Portsmouth Navy Yard (Portsmouth, NH / Kittery, ME), near his Portland, Maine station
letters.notes: Tom is 'sitting around doing nothing', walking 'around the yard', seeing movies and a USO show, and hasn't tried Portsmouth night life. There is a possibility of leave. Re-dated from the 1944 filename: in April 1944 Tom had just come back from the Pacific (see 1944-04-03), but the identical scan filed 450403 and the matching hospital-routine letters of April-May 1945 make 1945 more likely. Unconfirmed.

letters.location: A naval hospital (probably U.S. Naval Hospital, Portsmouth, NH)
letters.notes: KEY: Tom is a HOSPITAL PATIENT awaiting more tests, and doesn't yet know why he is there; others have been in six weeks or more. LANE IS A WOMAN ('on her way to Newark... how long she has to stay on the West Coast before taking off'), probably a Navy nurse or WAVE being transferred overseas (compare 1945-03-15, 'my entertainment committee... Lane is being transferred').

other_dates_mentioned: to-morrow (May 9, 1945) - trip to Portland for the car
'a week ago' (late April 1945) - sinking of a ship from his pier
letters.location: Naval hospital (probably Portsmouth, NH), 'down here' from Portland, Maine
letters.notes: Written on V-E Day while Tom listened to the radio all day and celebrated 'by staying in to-night'. He is still in the hospital with a daily routine of exercise, walks, and movies, and doesn't know when he'll be discharged. The doctor allowed a trip to Portland to fetch his car. A ship whose officers he knew, which tied up at his Portland pier, was sunk 'a week ago with very few survivors'; this is almost certainly USS Eagle 56 (PE-56), torpedoed off Portland, Maine on April 23, 1945 by U-853 with only 13 survivors. He was listening to 'Fibber McGee and Molly'.

letters.date_source: written as '23 May'; year 1945 from filename and content (hospital stay)
other_dates_mentioned: Sunday (May 20, 1945) - Red Sox(?) ball game in Boston
letters.location: Naval hospital (probably U.S. Naval Hospital, Portsmouth, NH) - Sick Officers' Quarters, moved to 'House 8'
letters.notes: KEY: THE HOSPITALIZATION WAS FOR MALARIA (almost certainly contracted in the South Pacific): 'the Malaria attack is over and that it is just a matter of waiting for the survey' (a medical survey board, which could lead to discharge; compare 'when I will be discharged', V-E Day letter). He moved from the SOQ (Sick Officers' Quarters) to House 8, the maternity ward for sick nurses and WAVES. He went to Boston for a ball game. Mr. West invited him to visit in Boston. 'Light pink, tinged with yellow' probably refers to atabrine (anti-malarial) skin yellowing.

letters.date_source: undated. A later annotation reads '? 5/30/45', but snow, ice skating, and basketball season, plus films released in late 1944 ('The Fighting Lady', 'Mrs. Parkington', 'Girl Rush'), point to winter 1944-45, most likely January-February 1945.
letters.location: Portland, Maine (Tom's phone is 'Portland 3-0411'); on duty 'aboard' the station
letters.notes: Typewritten in all capitals. Tom fixed water in the gas of his Chevrolet (the 'CHEV') himself by cleaning the carburetor and fuel pump. He is trying to quit smoking and to gain weight. Lane (with whom he goes out; see 1945-03-15 and 1945-04-30) had the duty. His new roommate is married. He has stopped worrying about orders: 'any duty in the States is good duty'. The 'Portland.jpg' file in the parent folder is this same page.

letters.date_source: undated ('Monday Eve 8:00'); two weeks into Army basic training in cold weather, probably winter 1942-43
letters.location: Co. F, 51st Engineers Combat Regt., Plattsburgh Barracks, New York
letters.notes: A family friend's thank-you to Mrs. Beck for popcorn. He also thanks Janny (cookies) and Isabel (post cards). 'I shall never forget all the Becks'. Bill Jameson/Jamison is almost certainly the 'Bill' who later married or became engaged to JANNY (see 1943-02-20 'How is Janny getting along without Bill', 1943-08-31 'Bill... once Janny has her mind set'); he sent Tom Christmas mail (1943-01-02) and was 'making the best of it' (1943-04-15). Tom Banks came to training with him. He hopes for officer training or the Air Force.

letters.date_source: undated ('Wednesday'); probably a January during Tom's Penn State years (late 1930s to 1941), since it refers to grades at 'State' and a Feb. 1 meeting in Philadelphia
letters.location: Written from home (Karns City, PA); Tom at Penn State ('State'); Tom and John planning a New York trip
letters.notes: This is a PRE-WAR letter FROM Tom's father. Dad was summoned to Philadelphia 'in connection with that oil investigation', which suggests Dad was in the oil business (consistent with the 'Co. trust', the lease, and Mother as company director). Dad writes warmly, promising a 'shout' if Tom passes and 'we just won't do any worrying' if not. John and Tom were headed to New York ('young bloods'). Dad banked for them.

letters.date_source: undated ('Wed. Afternoon'); from content, Tom's childhood, probably late 1920s
other_dates_mentioned: Saturday morning - Dad's return with a present
letters.location: Written from the Hotel St. George, Clark Street, Brooklyn, New York City, while Dad was traveling
letters.notes: A tender childhood letter: Dad is bringing Tommy 'something used in a baseball game' and will get Johnny (brother John) a glove. He describes a blue-eyed caddy who reminded him of Tommy, and says 'I am tickled that you are doing so well with your papers' (a paper route or schoolwork). Contains a period prejudiced remark about foreign caddies, transcribed as written. Filed with the Navy letters but pre-war.

letters.date_source: undated except 'Friday morning'; '1943' was added by a later hand. The start of a fall term, likely fall 1942 (George joined the Navy in mid-1943; see 1943-08-01)
letters.location: Allegheny College, Meadville, PA (per filename; 'Caflisch' and 'Brooks' are Allegheny College halls)
letters.notes: George writes from Allegheny College: a room mix-up in Caflisch Hall (room 43), a freshman dance in Brooks Hall with blind partners, and a comic hunt for a girl named Pat Painter. He asks for Bill's and Jim's addresses. This matches Tom's letters about George's grades, the draft, and his schooling (1943-02-03, 1943-04-15).

letters.date_source: undated ('Tuesday Morning'); the start of a fall term, while Dad was still living ('Daddy's car'), so probably Sept. 1941 or 1942
letters.location: PCW (per filename: Pennsylvania College for Women, now Chatham University, Pittsburgh; 'Shadyside' and '7th Ave.' are Pittsburgh references)
letters.notes: A letter from Tom's sister Janny at college: moving into her room, meeting her 'little sister', choosing Chemistry over Psychology for Home Ec, and asking for a chair, floor lamp, Bible, shoes, and tennis racquet from home. 'Billy'/'Bill' (probably Bill Jameson, whom Janny later married or became engaged to) drove her and took the 6:00 train. Mentions Phyllis, Peggy Bishop, Keith & Jean, Isabel's room, and John. A middle page seems to be missing; PG 4 duplicates PG 3.

letters.written_by: Mother (Elva Beck, Mrs. John A. Beck)
letters.written_to: 'Folks' (probably Tom and his wife/family, who had just visited - 'since you left')
letters.date_source: undated ('Moore Heights', Wednesday). The filename '4505moth' implies May 1945, but the content suggests Mother had recently moved into a new home ('Moore Heights', new fixtures, blacktopped driveway), possibly after the war.
letters.location: 'Moore Heights' (Mother's residence; location not stated, probably near Butler, PA)
letters.notes: This is the only letter in the collection written BY Tom's mother; it gives a sample of her handwriting and voice. She was at the Cavendish Club (a bridge club?), and mentions the Fairview family, Johnnie's speech, Bonnie (a grandchild?) who kissed her, Fred (who works for the government) installing light fixtures, Joan bringing her clock, Smitty with an insurance policy, Corbett blacktopping the driveway, Irene Deets, and Janny.
